brief: Judges a set of scoped rules two ways, against the cases they govern and against the questions a rule cannot ask of itself.
detail: Running a rule set asks whether the claim holds where the rule looked, never whether the rule looked in the right place. CheckRules asks that over a corpus of cases: a scope that selects nothing (scope_empty), a scope that selects every subject everywhere (scope_vacuous), a counter no case contains (boundary_unwitnessed), a rule with no claim (claim_unstated), two rules reaching for one subject with no declared precedence (subject_contested) and a rule reading a quantity that a later rule writes (read_is_stale). CheckCases is the ordinary half, the rules over the cases; CheckAll does both. A case is any object the scopes understand, a rendered diagram, a code graph, an org chart. StzPlasticGovernance is the graph plane's spelling.
receiver:
o1 = new stzRuleGovernance("numbers")
o2 = new stzScopedRule("all_small")
o2.SetClaim("every number is below 10")
o2.SetScope(func oL { return oL })
o2.SetClaimCheck(func oL, n { if n < 10  return [ 1, "" ]  ok  return [ 0, "it is " + n ] })
o1.AddRule(o2)
o1.AddCase("one", [ 1, 2, 3, 12 ])
o1.AddCase("two", [ 4, 6, 7 ])
